requirement_or_question: A reader that cannot verify a result must report it as unverified and never present unverified output as verified (I25). This binds every reader, CLI command and library result, including partial, remote, keyless-encrypted and salvage paths.
superseding_authority: docs/random-access-v1.md §Boundary L14-16; docs/inspection-explanation-v1.md §Inspection JSON L15-17 (refine I25 for partial and remote reads)
supersession_note: Repo docs refine I25 for random access (whole_archive_verified=false, PCI NotComputed) and remote inspect; no repo authority narrows I25.
implementation_evidence: Honoured: ecf/random.rs:40-47,958-991 (test unread_corrupt_chunk_does_not_create_a_whole_archive_claim random.rs:1333-1378); crypto/random.rs:1137-1170; entrybound-cli/src/lib.rs:3069-3104 read status. Gaps: identity.rs:77-83 VerificationState unused (cross-ref code-model-0129); no UNVERIFIED qualifier in diagnostics.rs:6-36 (cross-ref code-model-0159); ecf/random.rs:969-973 and crypto/random.rs:755-756 overclaim flags; archive/tooling.rs:1308-1324 unconditional 'whole archive verified'; lib.rs:4729-4753 keyless encrypted verify exits 0.
research_needed: Conformance matrix over every command and API against each verification scope (full, partial, remote, keyless, encrypted, salvage) asserting reported scope equals checks performed; mutation tests corrupting unread regions; simulated first-use interpretation study.
decision_needed: How is I25 enforced structurally (typed verification state versus report conventions) across all library and CLI outputs?

requirement_or_question: UNVERIFIED is a qualifier that may accompany an OK outcome, not a separate outcome class; 'read and fine' and 'read but could not check' must never be the same answer.
implementation_evidence: diagnostics.rs:6-36,346-382 define six OutcomeClass values and no UNVERIFIED qualifier (cross-ref code-model-0158, code-model-0159); 'PRIVATE CONTENT UNVERIFIED' exists only as CLI text (entrybound-cli/src/lib.rs:4750) with exit 0.
research_needed: Design and conformance tests for a typed qualifier carried through Diagnostic, JSON output and exit status; review of how scripts consume OK-with-qualifier.
decision_needed: How is the UNVERIFIED qualifier represented in diagnostics, JSON and exit status?

requirement_or_question: Each Reader result must carry whether its bytes were verified against a chunk digest, against a Merkle slice rooted in a signed PCR, or not at all, so callers never infer verification. How these three states map onto OK and OK+UNVERIFIED and onto reason codes is undefined.
implementation_evidence: identity.rs:77-83 defines VerificationState {ChunkVerified, PhysicalRootVerified, Unverified} but nothing uses it (cross-ref code-model-0129, access cluster); RandomAccessVerificationReport booleans and identity statuses carry scope instead (ecf/random.rs:72-95); no Merkle-slice verification exists (identity.rs:291-324,801-822; cross-ref code-model-0156).
research_needed: Type-level API design review with compile-fail tests proving unverified bytes cannot flow where verified bytes are required; mapping table from states to diagnostics; independent-reader check of the state model.
decision_needed: How do the three reader verification states map onto OK/OK+UNVERIFIED and typed library results?

requirement_or_question: verify output must state explicitly what was checked and what was not; a verify that did not decode chunk data must say so. Each printed verify claim (structure, sections, invariants, dependencies, chunk bytes, content, identities, LAI/PCR/AUX, PCI; STREAM framing, window, footer binding, length) must correspond to a detecting check.
superseding_authority: code:crates/entrybound-cli/src/lib.rs:4803-4818 (freezes the concrete unencrypted verify claim list)
supersession_note: Implementation freezes an explicit claim list for full verify; claims exist only for full decode verification because no lighter verify level exists.
implementation_evidence: entrybound-cli/src/lib.rs:4803-4818; tests cli_workflow.rs:30-32,152-156; corruption corpus ECF-F001..F015 in tests/native_ecf.rs:277-395 covers many claims; ContentDigestMismatch, ChunkRootMismatch and ChunkIdentityCollision are never asserted (code-model-0185..0187).
research_needed: Mutation/fuzz corpus mapping every printed claim to at least one corruption it detects; audit that no claim is printed for an unperformed check (encrypted, STREAM, remote).

requirement_or_question: SPEC: verify by default checks digests and structure; --deep decodes and verifies every chunk; unpack --verify-only decodes and verifies but writes nothing; a library verify returns a report without materializing. What default verify covers without decoding, for plaintext and for encrypted archives with or without identity, is unspecified; Research I left v1 verification modes unstated.
supersession_note: Code at 9e44608 (ecf/container.rs:1085-1102; entrybound-cli/src/lib.rs:4664-4708) collapses SPEC's default/--deep split into one full decode verification without an explicit freeze, so SPEC is not formally superseded.
implementation_evidence: ecf/container.rs:1085-1102 verify wraps full open; entrybound-cli/src/lib.rs:4664-4708 verify options are --signatures, --signature, --timestamp-trust, --require-*-signature, --identity, --password (no --deep/--against/--parity/--sidecar); unpack options lib.rs:2440-2519 lack --verify-only (cross-ref code-cli-0123); verify_with_limits returns VerificationReport without materializing.
research_needed: Measure time, RSS and bytes read for structure-only, stored-digest-only and full decode verification on large corpora; fault injection to establish which corruption classes each level detects; compare incumbent test modes (unzip -t, 7z t, zstd -t, restic check --read-data).
decision_needed: Which verification levels and modes are in v1 and what does each guarantee?

requirement_or_question: verify --against <dir|archive> checks that archive content matches a directory or another archive; Research I deferred a manifest-based verify-without-materializing mode to near-future scope.
supersession_note: SPEC §17.3 L1887 places --against in the v1 CLI synopsis, superseding Research I §17's near-future deferral; overlap with diff is unresolved (cross-ref ecosystem spec-06-0089).
implementation_evidence: verify has no --against option (entrybound-cli/src/lib.rs:4664-4708); archive_diff compares two fully verified archives (archive/tooling.rs:369-403, cross-ref code-fs-0139).
research_needed: Define compared tiers (LAI, AUX, per-entry bytes, metadata) and test against modified/renamed/extra files; CLI duplication analysis versus diff.
decision_needed: Should verify --against ship in v1, what equality does it assert, and how does it differ from diff?

requirement_or_question: PCI (SHA-256 over exact container bytes) is neither embedded nor signed, so verify can compute but not compare it without an externally supplied value. Container-digest verification before parsing (mirrors, CDNs, parser-differential defence) and verification without decoding are claimed needs that manifest identity alone cannot serve.
supersession_note: Repo docs say verify validates PCI; code only computes it, so 'validated' means 'computed'.
implementation_evidence: PCI computed while writing (ecf/stream.rs:856-870) and on read (ecf/stream.rs:2063-2104); random reads report PCI NotComputed (ecf/random.rs:40-47); no CLI option to supply an expected PCI (entrybound-cli/src/lib.rs:4664-4708).
research_needed: Use-case survey (package managers, mirrors, receipts, transparency logs) for container-digest checks; measure verify-by-hash versus verify-by-decode cost; parser-differential analysis of verifying bytes before parsing.
decision_needed: What does verifying PCI mean, may users supply an expected PCI or container digest checked before parsing, and is that required in v1?

requirement_or_question: Verification report booleans must reflect checks actually performed on objects actually exercised. INDEXED and STREAM reports hard-set every boolean true on success (failures abort), the unencrypted random report claims semantic metadata verified without fetching FIDELITY or verifying AUX, and encrypted range reports set dictionaries/groups verified from archive-wide feature presence.
implementation_evidence: ecf/container.rs:74-95,1049-1074; ecf/stream.rs:2106-2153 (test the_writer_is_deterministic_and_verification_is_repeatable stream_layout.rs:779-806); ecf/random.rs:969-973,209-241; crypto/random.rs:755-756,1144-1160; native_ecf.rs complete_in_memory_fixture asserts booleans (L153-156).
research_needed: Code audit mapping each flag to the check that sets it; mutation tests corrupting unread FIDELITY/dictionaries in random reads; cost (bytes, requests) of verifying FIDELITY/AUX in random reads.
decision_needed: Should reports carry per-check tri-state scoped to exercised objects, and should the random reader verify FIDELITY/AUX or narrow the flag meaning?

requirement_or_question: Inspection of a fully opened archive states 'whole archive verified', but what 'fully opened' entails is undefined. inspection_json prints VERIFIED and role Complete unconditionally, trusting callers to pass a fully verified OpenedArchive, and tooling indexes model maps directly, panicking on an unvalidated model.
implementation_evidence: archive/tooling.rs:1308,1311,1320-1324 unconditional strings; tooling.rs:1540,1584,2118-2141 direct map indexing; CLI local inspect fully verifies first (entrybound-cli/src/lib.rs:4161-4399, cross-ref code-cli-0170); remote inspection reports whole_archive_verified=false (tooling.rs:1736-1793, cross-ref code-fs-0166).
research_needed: Test that corrupting an unread payload never yields 'whole archive verified' from any path; fuzz inspection/explain with validated edge-case archives for panics; API review of whether OpenedArchive can be constructed without verification.
decision_needed: Should verification scope and role be carried in the OpenedArchive type so inspection cannot overstate scope?

requirement_or_question: Partial retrieval verifies the requested Chunks, their dependencies and ContentObject (chunk digests, chunk_root, logical digest, sparse map) plus fetched metadata identities, and never claims whole-archive PCR, PCI or segment-sequence verification. The status of encrypted reads that skip segment END and ArchiveFinal sequence verification is unspecified.
supersession_note: Repo docs freeze whole_archive_verified=false and PCI=NotComputed for every random read.
implementation_evidence: ecf/random.rs:186-241,566-600,815-846,40-47,958-991; crypto/random.rs:390-434,1137-1170,1881-1897; tests ecf/random.rs::unread_corrupt_chunk_does_not_create_a_whole_archive_claim (L1333-1378), crypto/random.rs::unread_encrypted_payload_corruption_does_not_become_a_whole_archive_claim (L2118-2184), entrybound-cli lib.rs::read_command_materializes_only_a_verified_indexed_entry (L6012-6083).
research_needed: Adversarial corpus tampering unread segments (delete, duplicate, reorder, splice sibling versions) confirming the requested result is unchanged or refused (cross-ref docs-access-0071, code-crypto-a-0120); formal model of partial-read guarantees; report-field audit per read.
decision_needed: What verification status is reported for encrypted random reads without full segment-sequence verification?

requirement_or_question: No range-based whole-archive verification exists: encrypted range readers never compute PCI or fully verify PCR, so whole-archive verification requires full download and open_encrypted; unencrypted INDEXED whole verification likewise requires a full in-memory open.
implementation_evidence: crypto/random.rs:1163-1167 (PCI NotComputed, PCR DeclaredNotFullyVerified); ecf/container.rs:1085-1102 full in-memory verify only.
research_needed: Measure bytes, requests and time for streaming whole-archive verification over HTTP ranges versus full download; determine whether PCR/PCI can be computed incrementally with bounded memory.
decision_needed: Is incremental remote whole-archive verification required for v1?

requirement_or_question: verify of an encrypted archive without unlock validates only public framing and digests, prints 'PRIVATE CONTENT UNVERIFIED' and exits 0; authenticated verification requires full unlock. Whether exit 0 misleads scripts, and whether keyless structural verification suffices for custodians without keys, are unresolved.
implementation_evidence: entrybound-cli/src/lib.rs:4729-4753; test crypto_cli.rs:81-85 asserts success; crypto/container.rs:653-658 verify_encrypted requires unlock; exit-code map lib.rs:4974-4991 (cross-ref code-cli-0005).
research_needed: Survey of CI/script handling of verify exit codes; simulated first-use evaluation of the output; review of incumbent exit semantics (gpg --verify, cosign verify, minisign).
decision_needed: Should unverified private content yield a non-zero or distinct exit status, and is keyless public verification a named verification level?

requirement_or_question: Unkeyed SHA-256 public section and segment-payload digests in encrypted archives are early corruption checks only, never a substitute for authentication; AEAD, SegmentEnd and ArchiveFinal provide security, and any footer locator or length used for acceptance must match the authenticated FooterCore.
source_location: New canonical record and section numbers L111-113
implementation_evidence: crypto/container.rs:1144-1153 unkeyed EncryptedSegments digest; tests crypto_v1.rs::commitment_envelope_ciphertext_footer_and_truncation_tampering_fail_closed (L395-443) rehash public digests before mutating ciphertext; ArchiveFinal/footer binding cross-ref docs-crypto-c-0220.
research_needed: Mutation corpus altering footer locators and lengths with recomputed unkeyed digests to confirm acceptance only through authenticated FooterCore; review of keyless-report wording so corruption checks are not described as authentication.

requirement_or_question: Truncation, corruption and unsupported features must be mutually distinguishable (I21), generalising the xz flags-CRC refinement; the distinction must survive every layer from record decoding to CLI exit status.
superseding_authority: docs/stream-layout-v1.md §Truncation versus corruption L246-256; docs/crypto-wire-v1.md ArchiveFinalV1 L646-648 (per-layout refinements)
supersession_note: Repo docs refine I21 separately for STREAM and encrypted INDEXED layouts.
implementation_evidence: diagnostics.rs:6-36 distinct classes; test native_ecf.rs::diagnostic_classes_remain_distinguishable (L784-799); exit codes 2/3/4 (entrybound-cli/src/lib.rs:4974-4991). Limits: record-level truncation is CORRUPT (canonical.rs:286-343, cross-ref code-model-0119); truncated preamble reuses TruncatedFooter (ecf/container.rs:2693-2706, cross-ref code-ecf-0100); crypto uses CORRUPT where docs name INTEGRITY_MISMATCH (cross-ref code-crypto-b-0058).
research_needed: Truncate-at-every-offset and region-targeted bit-flip corpora for INDEXED, STREAM and encrypted layouts tabulating OutcomeClass and reason code; combined unknown-feature plus truncation cases to fix precedence.
decision_needed: What is the precedence when truncation, corruption and unsupported features co-occur?

requirement_or_question: STREAM input ending inside the preamble, an item or before the footer is TRUNCATED; a complete footer declaring more bytes than read is TRUNCATED, fewer or trailing bytes is CORRUPT INCORRECT_TOTAL_LENGTH; an unrecognised boundary pattern is CORRUPT STREAM_ITEM_ORDERING. Footer recognition by non-seeking readers, cuts exactly at item boundaries, and appended or concatenated archives remain unspecified.
superseding_authority: docs/stream-layout-v1.md §Truncation versus corruption L246-256 (answers SPEC §3.9 I21 question for STREAM)
supersession_note: Repo STREAM layout resolves SPEC's open question with a fixed footer carrying body length and digest; concatenation semantics still open.
implementation_evidence: ecf/stream.rs:1896-1960; test stream_layout.rs::truncation_is_distinguishable_from_corruption (L393-431); CLI test cli_workflow.rs:246-275 (exit 3, TRUNCATED EB_ECF_TRUNCATED_STREAM).
research_needed: Conformance corpus: truncation at every byte and every item boundary, appended garbage, concatenated archives, footer magic embedded in item payloads; production versus independent-reader differential.
decision_needed: What exact state machine defines TRUNCATED versus CORRUPT for STREAM, including concatenated or appended input?

requirement_or_question: Truncation must be reported as truncated at N of M bytes with entries 1..k intact (TRUNCATED detail: declared length, actual length, last intact entry; Research I: report bytes written). The declared total length and manifest locators live in the trailing footer, which ordinary tail truncation removes, so readers cannot learn M or intact entries.
supersession_note: Structural contradiction inside SPEC (§4.4/§8.7/§20.5 versus trailer placement); code implements footer-based detection only.
implementation_evidence: ecf/container.rs:2880-2923 (footer <384 bytes or missing magic -> Truncated TruncatedFooter; declared > actual -> Truncated; declared < actual -> Corrupt); tests native_ecf.rs ECF-F004 (L305-314), truncated case (L402-404); no N-of-M or intact-entry detail (container.rs:2891-2899).
research_needed: Truncation corpus at every offset for INDEXED, STREAM and encrypted layouts measuring what a reader can recover and report without the trailer; evaluate leading declared length, periodic sync/checkpoint records and STREAM forward scan.
decision_needed: What mechanism supports truncation reports with intact-entry lists when the footer is missing?

requirement_or_question: Encrypted archives: a missing footer/EOF or an archive ending before a promised fragment, ciphertext or footer extent is TRUNCATED; a complete extent with a failed digest, tag, final marker or binding is an integrity failure; a complete authenticated object whose inner item length exceeds its bytes is NONCONFORMING.
implementation_evidence: Test crypto_v1.rs::commitment_envelope_ciphertext_footer_and_truncation_tampering_fail_closed (L395-443): commitment, envelope MAC and ciphertext mutations give typed codes; truncation gives TRUNCATED_FOOTER or INCORRECT_TOTAL_LENGTH; container diagnostics crypto/container.rs:2825-2839 (cross-ref code-crypto-a-0106).
research_needed: Pin one reason code per truncation offset (test currently accepts two; footer mutation asserts only is_err, cross-ref code-deps-tests-tools-0100); reconcile CORRUPT versus INTEGRITY_MISMATCH naming (code-crypto-b-0058); unify range and full reader footer codes (code-crypto-a-0150).

requirement_or_question: Full encrypted verification checks exact footer and EOF, public section digests, every segment's END transcript digest, ArchiveFinalV1 (segment and entry counts, logical bytes, unique chunks, LAI/PCR/AUX, recipient-set digest, prior segment-sequence digest, FooterCore digest, Descriptor and manifest IDs), EAM constraints, identities and PCI; negative vectors S5-S7 must be rejected as PRIVATE_OBJECT_INVALID.
supersession_note: Frozen crypto-v1 wire (docs/crypto-wire-v1.md) is the authority; no later override.
implementation_evidence: Tests crypto_v1.rs::recipient_and_segment_reordering_splicing_and_policy_limits_fail_closed and ::unknown_required_crypto_feature_fails_before_recipient_work (L445-585); ArchiveFinal/footer validation cross-ref docs-crypto-c-0220; vector helper emits S1-S7 (tools/crypto-vector-helper/src/main.rs:217-311).
research_needed: Exhaustive segment-level mutation corpus (every record header, END, ArchiveFinal field); independent-reader validation of S5-S7; truncation/splicing formal analysis in the crypto external-review dossier.

requirement_or_question: CORRUPT means structure or digest mismatch, with detail naming section, chunk, expected and actual digest. Every integrity failure (dictionary, prerequisite chunk, reconstruction data or region member, chunk, content, chunk root, entry identity/AUX, LAI/PCR/AUX) needs a stable typed code asserted by a conformance case.
implementation_evidence: diagnostics.rs:80-117,232-273 EB_INTEGRITY_* codes; asserted in native_ecf.rs ECF-F001..F015 (L277-395), cross_file_compression.rs (L75-97,190-240), jpeg_whole_object.rs (L77-198), reconstructive_transform.rs::missing_corrupt_or_undeclared_reconstruction_fails_typed (L98-137), compression_planner.rs::compressed_payload_and_plan_corruption_have_typed_failures (L295-347), cdc_dedup.rs (L163-173, names chunk). Unasserted: ContentDigestMismatch, ChunkRootMismatch; STREAM chunk-frame corruption asserts class only (stream_layout.rs:514-565); expected/actual digest detail not evidenced.
research_needed: Conformance case for every EB_INTEGRITY_* code; decide normative detail fields; independent-reader parity of codes; privacy review of digests in diagnostics for encrypted archives.
decision_needed: Which diagnostic detail fields are normative for CORRUPT and TRUNCATED outcomes?

requirement_or_question: Full native verification checks preamble and features, item framing and order, stored lengths, supporting-record and section digests before decode, dedup window, Dictionaries, ChunkGroups and reconstruction dependencies, every Chunk length and SHA-256, ContentObject digest and chunk_root, zero sparse holes, hardlink group digests, EAM invariants, budgets versus actuals, entry identities, LAI/PCR/AUX, footer binding, exact length and PCI.
implementation_evidence: identity.rs:244-289; ecf/stream.rs:1316-1333,1458-1492,1737-1768,1937-1960,2039-2104; ecf/container.rs:999-1000,3002-3008,3051-3088; tests stream_layout.rs::a_corrupted_supporting_record_is_caught_by_its_own_digest (L534-565), ::a_corrupted_chunk_payload_is_reported_as_corruption (L514-532); native_ecf.rs ECF-F009/F010 (L361-379); compression_planner.rs underdeclared requirements (L287-292).
research_needed: Mutation coverage report mapping each check to a failing test (content digest, chunk root, nonzero sparse hole and hardlink digest mismatches currently unasserted); sparse-hole verification cost on large sparse files; independent reader implementation.

requirement_or_question: Extraction and export fully verify before creating final objects: framing, every Chunk digest, ContentObject digests, EAM invariants, identity roots, footer binding and exact length are established before materialization, so unverified data never becomes a final file (unlike ZIP/tar streaming extractors). SPEC left open whether streaming extraction stages output or marks it unverified.
superseding_authority: docs/stream-layout-v1.md §Staging and safe extraction L371-374 (resolves SPEC §3.9 streaming question by staging)
supersession_note: Repo resolves SPEC's open streaming-extraction question by staging the whole STREAM before any materialization.
implementation_evidence: Encrypted unpack authenticates before extraction (entrybound-cli/src/lib.rs:2351-2372; test crypto_cli.rs:121-137); test filesystem_workflow.rs::corruption_and_policy_refusal_happen_before_materialization (L182-221); export content digest check legacy/export.rs:806-847.
research_needed: Fault injection at every region confirming zero destination writes; staging cost versus per-entry verified streaming for archives larger than RAM (cross-ref access cluster bounded staging).
decision_needed: Does extraction always stage until full verification, or may streaming extraction emit per-entry verified output before whole-archive roots are checked?

requirement_or_question: Derived artifacts (repack output, compressed tar export, migration targets, key and signature mutations) are reopened with the full strict reader and identity invariants checked before publication; LOSSLESS exports require strict re-import LAI equal to source LAI. LOSSY artifacts must differ only where typed issues predict, but that mechanism is not described.
implementation_evidence: Repack stages, syncs, re-verifies and hard-links (entrybound-cli/src/lib.rs:3476-3522); verify_mutation_output checks commitment, MAC, segments and EAM (crypto/container.rs:927-979); compressed-tar and migration re-import checks are doc statements without cited tests.
research_needed: Code review and tests of the LOSSY predicted-difference comparator; encoder fault injection confirming refusal to publish.
decision_needed: How is 'differs only where typed issues predict' mechanically verified for LOSSY exports?

requirement_or_question: Reconstructive transforms require SHA-256 and byte equality of recreated originals at write time, repeated by the ECF writer with no opt-out; readers reconstruct regions, slice by authoritative lengths and verify every original Chunk digest, and a region is unverified until all members pass. Write-time checks use the writer's own decoder, not independent decoders.
superseding_authority: docs/reconstructive-transform-v1.md §Exact verification L42-51; docs/jpeg-reconstruction-v1.md §Mandatory verification L64-90 (refine SPEC §5.6 and I31)
supersession_note: Repo docs make writer re-verification mandatory and non-disableable; SPEC's independent-decoder concern remains open.
implementation_evidence: ecf/container.rs:2277-2335 exact region length and member digests; tests jpeg_whole_object.rs ECF-REGION-* cases (L77-198), reconstructive_transform.rs::missing_corrupt_or_undeclared_reconstruction_fails_typed (L98-137).
research_needed: Differential decoding against independent preflate and JPEG XL implementations; cross-build/platform vectors; real-world corpus success rates (compression Task 8.8); tests that API paths injecting precomputed plans are re-verified.
decision_needed: Must registered reconstructive transforms carry test vectors proving cross-decoder determinism?

requirement_or_question: Decoders validate parameters and caller memory policy before dispatch, allocate only declared output, reject trailing or malformed payloads and length mismatch, then verify plaintext digests; declared lengths are bounded untrusted hints until authenticated. STREAM chunk frames carry no stored-bytes digest, so codecs see unauthenticated input, and zstd decode may accept concatenated or skippable frames despite documented rejection.
implementation_evidence: codec.rs:982-1013 bulk and prefix zstd decode without leftover-byte check (no test of trailing frames); test compression_planner.rs::compressed_payload_and_plan_corruption_have_typed_failures (L295-347); limits checked 'where available' (docs/reconstructive-transform-v1.md L106-109).
research_needed: Craft payloads with trailing skippable and data frames and extra bytes for every codec; fuzz decode paths under memory ceilings with lying lengths; compare STREAM decode-before-integrity with INDEXED section-digest-first behaviour.
decision_needed: Must stored payloads be canonical single frames with no trailing bytes, and should STREAM frames carry a stored-bytes digest checked before decoding?

requirement_or_question: A digest collision between different captured bytes is a typed failure (ChunkIdentityCollision) and similarity is never proof of equality; replanning rejects plaintext whose digest differs from its ContentObject or distinct plaintext under one chunk ID.
implementation_evidence: archive/filesystem.rs:257-317 (ContentDigestMismatch, ChunkIdentityCollision); no test asserts ChunkIdentityCollision (diagnostics.rs:110,266).
research_needed: Conformance case triggering ChunkIdentityCollision via a crafted model; confirm the writer byte-compares on dedup hits and measure the retention cost.

requirement_or_question: Index damage never changes semantics: an absent Index yields RebuiltAbsent; payload digest mismatch, noncanonical records or locator differences yield RebuiltInvalid with locators rebuilt from CHUNK_DATA; STREAM has no Index. Yet a damaged INDEX section header (magic, id, version, flags, reserved bytes, overrunning length) is a fatal structural error.
superseding_authority: docs/format-v0.md §Index handling L467-475 (implements SPEC §4.5 L425 and I10)
implementation_evidence: ecf/container.rs:2539-2580,63-72,2960-3008; tests native_ecf.rs::index_is_optional_and_never_changes_semantics (L242-265) and invalid-Index corpus case (L406-409); no test of Index header damage.
research_needed: Mutation experiment on Index header versus payload bytes tabulating outcomes; security analysis of ignoring a damaged trailing section.
decision_needed: Should a reader ignore a structurally damaged trailing INDEX section instead of rejecting the archive?

requirement_or_question: Per-section digests are claimed to localise a damaged section without a full scan. Unencrypted INDEXED binds only section payload SHA-256s and a preamble-bound footer: section headers and the footer have no digest, so header, length-field or footer-locator damage relies on downstream checks and can break traversal of later sections.
implementation_evidence: ecf/container.rs:2850-2869,3002-3008 payload digests only; STREAM footer binds a STREAM_BODY digest (ecf/stream.rs:1937-1960) with no INDEXED equivalent.
research_needed: Fault injection on section headers, length fields and footer bytes measuring detection, diagnostic precision and sections still localisable; differential fuzzing for undetected reinterpretation via header or boundary manipulation.
decision_needed: Should the INDEXED footer bind a digest over the section header chain or carry a self-checksum?

requirement_or_question: verify on a damaged archive must report failing chunks, their ContentObjects, referencing Entries, entries affected through group dependency, and which entries are intact; localisation should work without reading the whole archive when an Index is present. Current readers are fail-fast: the first diagnostic aborts with no multi-error collection or per-entry localisation.
implementation_evidence: ecf/container.rs:830-1075 fail-fast open/verify; diagnostics name only the first failing section or chunk (cdc_dedup.rs:163-173).
research_needed: Corruption injection (bit flips, bursts, missing chunks, section, Index and footer damage) comparing reported damaged, affected and intact sets with ground truth; bytes read with and without Index; resource bounds of continue-on-error.
decision_needed: Must v1 verify continue past the first failure to produce a damage map, or does localisation belong only to salvage?

requirement_or_question: SPEC §7.5 says a damaged chunk destroys its group's dependent chunks while §8.7 narrows this to at most k following chunks. Code classifies a decode or digest failure of a chunk that later group members depend on within max_lookback as PrerequisiteChunkCorrupt. Solid RAR archives lose every following file; content lost per corrupt prerequisite in Entrybound is unmeasured.
supersession_note: Code (ecf/container.rs:1978-2007,2525-2537) implements a direct-lookback prerequisite classification without an explicit freeze and without resolving SPEC's k-following versus whole-group wording.
implementation_evidence: ecf/container.rs:1994-2007,1978-1992,2525-2537; tests cross_file_compression.rs PrerequisiteChunkCorrupt (L190-240, L386), native_ecf.rs ECF-F010 (L370-379).
research_needed: Quantify logical bytes and entries made unreadable by one corrupt chunk across lookback 0/1/2/4/8 and dictionary use (Task 8.5 corruption propagation); formal definition of transitive dependency closure.
decision_needed: Is corruption blast radius defined as k following chunks, the transitive dependency closure, or the whole group, and how is it reported?

requirement_or_question: SPEC's matrix claims full corruption localisation for Entrybound (full for RAR5, xz, DwarFS, Apple; partial for uncompressed tar, zstd, squashfs, OCI; absent for ZIP, 7z, gzip). The appendix asserts compressed tar loses everything downstream, zstd frames and xz block checks with an Index localise damage, and per-block checks plus an index are the realistic no-parity middle ground.
supersession_note: Cross-ref ecosystem spec-03-0224 (same incumbent damage-tolerance claim).
implementation_evidence: none found: no localisation report exists (ecf/container.rs:830-1075 fail-fast) and no measurement.
research_needed: Corruption-injection experiment: entries and bytes lost per damaged byte and per burst length for Entrybound profiles and lookback settings versus tar, tar.gz, tar.zst, xz, zip, 7z, RAR5 and squashfs.

requirement_or_question: Entrybound is designed to answer which entries are damaged, not to survive damage; surviving damage is deliberately left to other tools. The supporting assertion that users need precise damage assessment rather than repair is unsupported.
supersession_note: In-format damage survival is refused; external-parity repair remains required (see external-parity rows).
implementation_evidence: No in-format recovery exists (no recovery sections; cross-ref code-ecf-0014).
research_needed: Incident and user evidence (bug trackers, forums, restore reports) on repair versus assessment needs; simulated first-use evaluation.
decision_needed: Is 'assessment, not survival' validated by user evidence, or must v1 provide repair?

requirement_or_question: Truncation is asserted to be the dominant real-world archive failure mode, one no incumbent handles well and a leading magic alone cannot detect.
implementation_evidence: Capability concerned (truncation detection) is partial: footer-based detection only (ecf/container.rs:2880-2923; ecf/stream.rs:1896-1936).
research_needed: Empirical failure-mode data (interrupted downloads, disk-full, bit rot, latent sector errors, transfer mangling) from bug trackers, storage field studies and package-manager incidents; incumbent truncation behaviour tests.

requirement_or_question: Salvage and repair semantics for damaged encrypted archives are undefined; commitment, envelope or encrypted Index damage may make all content unrecoverable, and whether intact records can be extracted when a segment END, envelope or Index is corrupt is unspecified.
implementation_evidence: none found: encrypted readers are fail-closed (tests crypto_v1.rs:395-585); no salvage command (entrybound-cli/src/lib.rs:306-310).
research_needed: Corruption injection per encrypted structure (commitment, envelope, recipient directory, encrypted descriptor/Index, segment END, ArchiveFinal, footer) measuring entries recoverable with keys; interaction with external parity.
decision_needed: What salvage guarantees apply to damaged encrypted archives?

requirement_or_question: salvage <archive.eb> [destination] with --best-effort and --report <file> recovers what can be recovered and reports what was recovered and lost; it exists because §11.4 and §22.5 reference it normatively (§11.4 wrongly cites §17.4). Incumbent recovery is weak: zip -F/-FF need or scan structures, 7-Zip recovery is manual hex editing.
supersession_note: SPEC review pass 1 added salvage/repair; code at 9e44608 has no salvage command (treated as a future command in a unit test) and no repo authority defers it.
implementation_evidence: entrybound-cli/src/lib.rs:306-310 returns EB_CLI_NOT_IMPLEMENTED; unit test future_commands_fail_explicitly (lib.rs:5539-5543); dispatcher lib.rs:286-311 (cross-ref code-cli-0008); no salvage reason codes (cross-ref code-model-0175).
research_needed: Damaged-archive corpora measuring salvage recovery rate, false-recovery rate and report accuracy versus zip -FF, 7-Zip and RAR repair; fix the §11.4 cross-reference.
decision_needed: Will salvage ship in v1, and what does it do without --best-effort?

requirement_or_question: Recovery is a separate, explicitly labelled operation whose outputs are marked unverified in the report and in-band where the destination allows; salvage never claims a signature or the archive verified. The in-band marker mechanism per destination type (xattr, alternate stream, suffix, marker file) is unspecified.
supersession_note: PROGRAM Task 24 restates that salvage never implies verification.
implementation_evidence: none found (salvage absent: entrybound-cli/src/lib.rs:306-310).
research_needed: Platform feasibility and copy survival of in-band markers (xattrs, NTFS ADS, suffixes, manifest files) across cp, rsync, zip and cloud sync; conformance test that no salvage path emits VERIFIED.
decision_needed: Which in-band unverified marker is used per destination type, and how is it prevented from being dropped?

requirement_or_question: salvage is the only command that produces output from a non-conforming archive, which lets unpack, list and verify stay strict. ZIP has no recoverability (central-directory loss is often fatal; tools scan local headers), raising whether salvage should extend to legacy inputs.
implementation_evidence: Strict fail-fast readers exist (ecf/container.rs:830-1075; native corpus rejections native_ecf.rs:277-410; filesystem_workflow.rs::corruption_and_policy_refusal_happen_before_materialization L182-221); ZIP import is all-or-nothing (cross-ref docs-legacy-0031); no salvage path.
research_needed: Run unpack, list, verify, inspect, read and diff over every nonconforming corpus case asserting refusal; evaluate ZIP local-header scan salvage against legacy strict-import doctrine.
decision_needed: Should a legacy ZIP local-header scan salvage mode exist?

requirement_or_question: In-archive recovery records and error correction are refused (disposition 5 Reject, 'permanently refused', though listed under a 'deferred rather than refused' heading): parity belongs outside the archive, and a recovery decoder inside the archive parser is attack surface, as the WinRAR 7.23 RAR5 recovery-volume heap overflow showed.
implementation_evidence: No recovery/ECC section or code path exists (cross-ref code-ecf-0014 section list).
research_needed: Primary citations (CVE ids, affected versions) for recovery-parser vulnerabilities; comparative recovery effectiveness of in-format versus external parity under identical damage; resolve the SPEC §24 categorisation inconsistency.
decision_needed: Is in-archive error correction a permanent, evidence-confirmed non-goal or a deferred matter?

requirement_or_question: External parity is claimed to compose and age better than in-format parity: it protects any file, redundancy is chosen or topped up after creation and kept on other media, the ECC decoder stays out of the archive parser, and a separate parity artifact over a canonical archive is the strong default when recovery is required.
implementation_evidence: none found: no parity binding, verify --parity or repair command (entrybound-cli/src/lib.rs:286-311,4664-4708).
research_needed: Operational study of managing parity sidecars (loss, separation, mismatch); recovery effectiveness versus RAR5 recovery records at equal overhead; threat analysis of external parity decoders.

requirement_or_question: A normative binding must let verify <archive> --parity <file> and repair <archive> --parity <file> [--out <file>] work with a mature parity format as a first-class workflow. Unspecified: parity format, bound identity (PCI, LAI, signature), authentication, discovery, verification of repaired output, and in-place behaviour without --out; loosely coupled sidecars are separated by unaware copy tools.
implementation_evidence: No repair command or --parity option (entrybound-cli/src/lib.rs:286-311,4664-4708; code-cli-0227 records no parity/ECC binding commands).
research_needed: Research-tooling prototype binding over PAR2 and alternatives; separation and mismatch detection through cp, rsync, zip, HTTP upload/download and object stores; parity-file damage cases.
decision_needed: Which parity format and binding identity are normative, how is the binding authenticated and discovered, and does repair without --out modify the archive atomically?

requirement_or_question: Error correction must never launder corruption into a trusted read: as with dm-verity FEC, every repaired block must be re-verified against authenticated digests (chunk IDs, section digests, identity roots, signatures) before being reported valid, and repair output is verified by the full reader before publication.
supersession_note: Consistent with repo publish-after-reverify pattern (docs/repack-v1.md §Verification and publication L32-34).
implementation_evidence: none found (no repair path).
research_needed: Tests injecting wrong parity reconstructions and confirming refusal; re-verification cost measurement.

requirement_or_question: Candidate parity formats as of 2026-08-29: PAR2 (Reed-Solomon over GF(2^16), finalised, par2cmdline 1.1.1 maintained); PAR3 (stalled 2022 alpha, pluggable codes, Blake3 packets, InputSetID, dedup, archive-like scope); RaptorQ (RFC 6330 rateless fountain code designed for networks, allows redundancy top-up; licensing unassessed); zfec (status unverified).
implementation_evidence: none found.
research_needed: Re-verify statuses; evaluate Rust implementations, licences and patents (RaptorQ), maintenance, recovery-versus-overhead curves under scattered and burst damage, and decoder hardening (fuzz PAR2 parsers).

requirement_or_question: SPEC marks error correction absent for Entrybound, best-in-class for RAR5 and full for Apple AA, while §22.3/§22.5 say only RAR5 ships it. Appendix: RAR5 recovery records up to 1000% plus .rev volumes; Apple Archive lists an undocumented ECC field; WIM has optional SHA-1 integrity tables; xz, ZIP, 7z, tar and zstd only detect; OCI detects without repair; RAR effectiveness depends on record size and damage pattern.
supersession_note: SPEC internal contradiction on Apple AA ECC (§22.2 L2373/L2379 versus §22.3 L2389).
implementation_evidence: Entrybound in-archive ECC refused (see in-archive-ecc-refused); no code.
research_needed: Verify Apple Archive ECC presence and algorithm; test RAR5 recovery limits with rar 7.x under scattered and burst damage; update the incumbent matrix with primary citations.

requirement_or_question: The preamble declares the archive role (Complete, Sidecar, Incremental) so a reader can refuse a non-extractable archive before doing anything; role values and their effect on verification and extraction must be defined. At 9e44608 only Complete exists: model enum, validation, container reader and inspect accept only role 1.
superseding_authority: docs/format-v0.md §Container L40-41 (only Complete implemented; LAI binds Complete)
supersession_note: Repo narrows SPEC §8.5's three roles to Complete; this is a current-scope statement, not an explicit deferral or rejection.
implementation_evidence: eam/model.rs:37-42 ArchiveRole::Complete only; eam/validate.rs:97-103 non-Complete is Unsupported EB_ECF_UNSUPPORTED_REQUIRED_FEATURE; ecf/container.rs:2766-2772 'only Complete bootstrap archives are supported'; entrybound-cli/src/lib.rs:4164-4169 single match arm; cross-ref model spec-03-0204, container spec-03-0068.
research_needed: Conformance cases with role bytes 2, 3 and unknown asserting classification before any other processing; spec definition of per-role reader behaviour.
decision_needed: Which archive roles ship in stable v1, and how does each change reader behaviour?

requirement_or_question: Encrypted crypto-v1 archives must be Complete-role INDEXED: encrypted incremental or partial archives with base chains or external content references are excluded, encrypted archives cannot use compatible feature bits or a public resource budget, and key hierarchy across base chains is unaddressed.
source_location: Algorithms and enums L42-43; Encrypted INDEXED container L133

additional_sources.location: docs/crypto-threat-model-v1.md §Scope and protected assets L12; docs/crypto-suite-v1.md §CryptoEnvelope authentication L143-146

supersession_note: Frozen crypto-v1 wire fixes role 1 in commitment and public context (cross-ref code-crypto-b-0041, docs-crypto-b-0020).
implementation_evidence: crypto/container.rs:1081-1086 requires Complete role; crypto/mod.rs:455,485-486 (cross-ref).
research_needed: Demand assessment for encrypted incremental backups; design review of AFK/key-domain sharing across base chains, dedup-domain leakage and recipient-set interaction (cross-ref crypto spec-04-0090).
decision_needed: Will encrypted non-Complete roles be supported after v1, under which feature or version, and with what key-domain model?

requirement_or_question: Binding archive role into LAI prevents a signed Complete archive from being stripped of its content and still verifying as a valid signed archive, for example relabelled as a content-free Sidecar with the same LAI.
supersession_note: Cross-ref crypto spec-03-0205 (same closure stated in §8.5 L963).
implementation_evidence: LAI hashes role byte 1 (identity.rs:503-536, cross-ref code-model-0145); no other role is representable, so the attack path is not exercised.
research_needed: Attack tests converting Complete archives to Sidecar/Incremental once roles exist; formal model of signature coverage over LAI (role, entry count, logical size) and ContentRef kind; independent security review of role confusion.
decision_needed: Is role participation in LAI, with ContentRef kind in entry identity, sufficient against content-stripping and role-confusion attacks?

requirement_or_question: ContentRef is a two-variant sum: Internal {content_object_id} or External {digest, length, optional locator}, claimed to be a small, well-contained addition serving sidecars, incremental archives referencing a base, and Stage-2 adoption for artifacts still published as ZIP. At 9e44608 only Internal exists in model, wire and export.
implementation_evidence: eam/model.rs:93-98 ContentRef::Internal only; ecf/records.rs:1054-1058,1198-1200 wire Internal only; legacy/export.rs:807 irrefutable Internal destructure.
research_needed: Design review of External refs across verify, unpack, list, diff, salvage, export, repack, random access and budget declaration to test the 'well-contained' claim; canonical encoding vectors; digest agility for External.digest.
decision_needed: Is the External ContentRef variant in stable v1?

requirement_or_question: External.locator is optional, but its syntax (URL, relative path), whether it participates in LAI, and the security policy for resolving it (remote fetch, path traversal, confinement, advisory-only use) are unspecified.
implementation_evidence: none found (no External ContentRef: eam/model.rs:93-98).
research_needed: Security review of locator resolution; scenarios: mirror URL change, renamed or moved originals, relative-path escape, hostile redirects; signature stability under locator edits.
decision_needed: Is the locator excluded from identity and advisory-only, and may readers dereference local or remote locators automatically?

requirement_or_question: Behaviour of unpack, list, diff, export, salvage and repack on Sidecar (content-less) archives or External refs is unspecified: refuse, resolve through locator or base, or preserve references. Repack is limited to Complete archives, and whether it must resolve or preserve base references is unspecified.
supersession_note: Cross-ref access docs-access-0003 (random access Complete-only).
implementation_evidence: docs/repack-v1.md Status L3-4 limits repack to Complete; no non-Complete roles exist (eam/model.rs:37-42).
research_needed: Per-command behaviour matrix with failure scenarios (missing, stale or mismatched base) and conformance cases.
decision_needed: Do content-consuming commands refuse Sidecar/Incremental archives, resolve External refs, or preserve them, and with what verification?

requirement_or_question: An Incremental archive references a base and requires it for extraction; external references let it reuse a base without copying, claimed better than append because the result is complete and verifiable, without making an archive a repository. Base identifier (LAI, PCR, PCI), chain depth, ordering in identity (cf. OCI ChainID) and base-binding verification are unspecified; cross-archive dedup is unsupported.
supersession_note: Repo status excludes cross-archive dedup; no repo authority schedules incremental archives.
implementation_evidence: No incremental, base-chained, append or update commands (entrybound-cli/src/lib.rs:286-311); no Incremental role or External refs (eam/model.rs:37-42,93-98).
research_needed: Research prototype of incremental archives over External refs; scenarios: missing, substituted, stale and multiple bases, cycles, depth; size of incremental versus full repack versus append formats.
decision_needed: By which identity is a base referenced, what verification precedes extraction, and how are chains ordered, bounded and cycle-checked?

requirement_or_question: Review pass 1 fixed that external references voided losslessness and enabled content deletion on signed archives: archive role is declared and identity-participating, and the byte-exact losslessness contract is scoped to Complete archives. Whether extracting an Incremental with all bases present and verified carries the same guarantee is unstated.
implementation_evidence: Only Complete is representable (eam/model.rs:37-42) so the contract holds trivially; LAI binds role byte (identity.rs:503-536, cross-ref code-model-0145).
research_needed: Specify and test losslessness for Incremental extraction with verified base chains, including base substitution and stale-base round trips.
decision_needed: Does the losslessness contract extend to Incremental archives when all bases are available and verified?

requirement_or_question: Incremental or layered archives must represent entry deletion sensibly (tar and OCI whiteouts grow size and reserve names); how an Entrybound incremental archive represents deletions is not addressed.
source_location: §4 What tar gets wrong L295, L297
supersession_note: Cross-ref legacy code-legacy-a-0137 (7z anti-items refused on import).
implementation_evidence: none found; 7z anti-items refused (legacy/sevenz.rs:1822-1826, cross-ref).
research_needed: Compare tombstone entries, whiteouts, opaque directories, 7z anti-items and full-manifest incrementals for size, reserved-name conflicts and identity semantics.
decision_needed: How does an Incremental archive represent entry deletion without reserved names or size growth?

requirement_or_question: No external dependency is structural for a Complete archive: no network service, key server or registry lookup is required to decode a Complete archive you hold.
implementation_evidence: ContentRef is Internal only (eam/model.rs:93-98); offline generated RFC 3161 verification test exists (cross-ref docs-crypto-c-0238); no network-isolated decode conformance run found.
research_needed: Network-namespace-isolated decode and verify conformance run; separate decode dependencies from signature and timestamp trust validation.

requirement_or_question: Network-backed archives (content living elsewhere) are expressible through external references, but no fetch protocol is specified in v1; resolution and authentication of fetched content remain open.
implementation_evidence: none found; HTTP range access exists only for reading a whole .eb archive (cross-ref access cluster random_access.rs).
research_needed: Threat model for fetched external content (digest authentication, advisory locators, SSRF and privacy leakage); feasibility over HTTP ranges and object stores.
decision_needed: Will a fetch/resolution protocol for external references be specified after v1, and how is fetched content authenticated and policy-gated?

requirement_or_question: verify release.zip --sidecar release.zip.eb checks a legacy artifact against its sidecar description. Repo sidecars are native archives whose authenticated ConversionProvenance source digest must equal SHA-256 of the exact legacy input before publication; detecting later drift of the legacy file and sidecars for --entry-name stream inputs are undescribed.
supersession_note: Repo sidecars are content-bearing Complete-role archives with exact-source digest binding, not SPEC §15.4 content-free role=Sidecar archives with External refs; verify has no --sidecar option.
implementation_evidence: Sidecar publish reopens and checks provenance binding (entrybound-cli/src/lib.rs:1818-1896; unit test sidecar_binds_exact_legacy_source_and_verifies_before_publish lib.rs:5804-5897, cross-ref code-cli-0114); verify options lack --sidecar (lib.rs:4664-4708).
research_needed: Workflow tests with modified, renamed and truncated legacy files versus sidecars; size overhead of content-bearing versus content-free sidecars; copy-tool separation.
decision_needed: Should v1 sidecars be content-free role=Sidecar archives or content-bearing provenance-bound archives, and should verify check a legacy file against its sidecar?

requirement_or_question: Research I made backup semantics (dedup, incremental, snapshotting) a non-goal and far-future scope. Repository designs show what such semantics entail: Borg 2 object stores without refcounts, soft delete with compact/undelete, Kopia epoch indexes with deterministic merge, Duplicacy two-step fossil GC.
superseding_authority: SPEC §24 item 3 L2505 and §8.5 L957-961 (Incremental role admitted; archives are not repositories)
supersession_note: SPEC supersedes Research I's blanket incremental non-goal by admitting Incremental roles while keeping repository, snapshot and GC semantics out of scope.
implementation_evidence: none found (no repository, GC or snapshot code).
research_needed: Confirm where the SPEC records the boundary between Incremental archives and repository semantics; document how backup tools layer on Entrybound.
decision_needed: Has the later design explicitly superseded Research I's backup non-goal, and where is the Incremental-versus-repository boundary recorded?

requirement_or_question: A versioned-log model (append-only journal with rollback to prior states, e.g. zpaq writing a temporary header, appending data and index, then rewriting the header so interrupted appends are ignored) is a plausible future extension and v1 non-goal, not a permanent refusal.
supersession_note: Cross-ref container spec-07-0226 (append-in-place rejected).
implementation_evidence: No append or update commands (entrybound-cli/src/lib.rs:286-311).
research_needed: Demand evidence; crash-safety comparison of journaling commit protocols.
decision_needed: Under what conditions would a crash-safe versioned-journal extension be designed?

requirement_or_question: Flat per-chunk digests (cheap sequential verification) and a Merkle tree (O(log n) random verification against a signed root) are both required. Candidates: flat digest list trusted through a verified index (eStargz two-stage), balanced Merkle outboard (Bao, fs-verity), sizes sister-list DAG (UnixFS); hash chains (AEA) force linear walks. The container serialises no outboard tree.
implementation_evidence: Per-chunk frame chunk_id and ContentObject chunk_root recomputed from the full leaf list; no MERKLE_OUTBOARD section or proof API (ecf/container.rs:2595-2621; ecf/records.rs:903-915; cross-ref code-model-0156, code-ecf-0014).
research_needed: Measure verify-one-range cost (bytes fetched, requests, RAM, CPU) for flat list, outboard and sister-list at 10^6-10^9 chunks under signature; index-trust requirements (container Task 11).
decision_needed: Is MERKLE_OUTBOARD required in v1, or do flat chunk digests plus authenticated ContentObject leaf lists suffice for remote partial verification?

requirement_or_question: 'Consistent by construction' holds only for honest writers: in a crafted archive flat chunk-table digests and MERKLE_OUTBOARD can disagree, and which is authoritative or whether readers must cross-check is unstated.
implementation_evidence: none found (no outboard serialised, so no disagreement path exists yet).
research_needed: Conformance corpus with inconsistent flat digests versus tree; outcome equality across full, range and independent readers.
decision_needed: Which structure is authoritative and what must a conforming reader do on disagreement?

requirement_or_question: chunk_root is a Merkle root over the chunk list feeding PCR and signed objects, giving range readers an authenticated root. Trees must domain-separate leaves and nodes, never duplicate odd final nodes, split at the largest power of two without padding, length-prefix multi-field inputs, and bind leaf count or length so truncated trees are invalid; BLAKE3's internal tree is an alternative.
superseding_authority: docs/format-v0.md §Digests L215-217 (domain separation, largest-power-of-two split, no padding; cross-ref docs-format-0069)
supersession_note: Repo freezes an explicit SHA-256 tree with named domains instead of BLAKE3's tree.
implementation_evidence: identity.rs:291-324 leaves H('chunk-tree/leaf', chunk_id, u64 logical_len) with empty and node domains; identity.rs:801-822 largest-power-of-two split, no padding (cross-ref code-model-0137/0138); chunk count bound only through PCR/LAI descriptors (cross-ref spec-03-0203).
research_needed: Independent recomputation vectors; tests that distinct odd-length and truncated leaf lists give distinct roots and subtrees cannot pose as leaves; documented rationale for the SHA-256 tree over BLAKE3's tree.
decision_needed: Is the explicit SHA-256 tree free of known Merkle pitfalls, with chunk count bound where range readers need it, and is rejecting BLAKE3's tree documented?

requirement_or_question: Inclusion and range proofs could be emitted as RFC 9942 COSE Receipts (RFC9162_SHA256 tree, inclusion label -1, consistency label -2) to join the SCITT ecosystem rather than inventing a proof encoding; RFC 9942 does not define Merkle Mountain Range proofs.
implementation_evidence: none found (no proof API: identity.rs:291-324,801-822).
research_needed: Assess tree-shape compatibility of Entrybound roots with RFC 9162 hashing; demand from supply-chain transparency workflows.
decision_needed: Should Entrybound inclusion or range proofs be exportable as COSE Receipts?

requirement_or_question: Content-only verity (fs-verity) protects file bytes but not names or directory structure; Entrybound's verified roots must cover logical paths, entry kinds, tree structure and identity-bearing metadata, not only content.
implementation_evidence: Entry identity binds path components, kind, ContentRef kind, logical digest and core.executable, and the manifest root over identity digests feeds LAI (identity.rs:503-536; cross-ref docs-format-0138, code-model-0145); corpus cases ECF-F011 and ECF-F014 detect LAI and entry identity mismatch (native_ecf.rs:277-395).
research_needed: Mutation tests renaming entries, changing kinds and reordering trees with recomputed section digests; confirm AUX-only metadata (mtime, xattrs) is detected through AUX.

requirement_or_question: The FidelityReport is in-band and typed, not a log; it is covered by the AUX digest and any signature, and queryable via inspect --fidelity.
implementation_evidence: AUX includes H('fidelity/v1', fidelity) (identity.rs:562-602, cross-ref code-model-0147); inspect prints fidelity classes (entrybound-cli/src/lib.rs:4310-4381, cross-ref code-cli-0182) but has no --fidelity option (lib.rs:3920-3942, cross-ref code-cli-0168); the unencrypted random reader neither fetches FIDELITY nor verifies AUX (ecf/random.rs:209-241); ECF-F013 AuxMismatch corpus case (native_ecf.rs).
research_needed: FidelityReport tamper test with recomputed section digest; decide whether random reads verify AUX.

requirement_or_question: In adaptive mode the planner may use the real environment; the archive records that it did, and verify --reproducible reports it as adaptively planned rather than failing an unwinnable reproduction comparison.
implementation_evidence: verify has no --reproducible option (entrybound-cli/src/lib.rs:4664-4708).
research_needed: Define what reproduction verification re-plans and compares (PCR, PCI); cross-platform determinism runs (Task 14).
decision_needed: Does verify --reproducible ship, how is adaptive planning recorded, and what does reproduction verification compare?

requirement_or_question: Verification reports each signature binding (content, physical, addressing) separately: the signature is checked over stored values first (bad signature is INVALID); each present binding is VALID if current, STALE (not forged) if verified but differing, or ABSENT; stale bindings fail only under caller policy, and a stale physical binding falls back to the archive's unsigned PCR.
superseding_authority: docs/crypto-suite-v1.md §Signatures L670-676, §Timestamps L717-719; docs/crypto-wire-v1.md Stable diagnostic taxonomy L789-791
supersession_note: Repo docs define the STALE-versus-INVALID rule SPEC §9.6 left open.
implementation_evidence: CLI prints cryptographic VALID/INVALID/UNSUPPORTED and bindings VALID/STALE/NOT_BOUND (entrybound-cli/src/lib.rs:4856-4900, cross-ref code-cli-0199); BindingStatus lacks INVALID, so a failed Ed25519 check reports bindings STALE (crypto/signature.rs:401-435,520-536, cross-ref code-crypto-b-0077); policy flags --require-*-signature (lib.rs:4664-4708).
research_needed: Conformance tests per status; simulated first-use evaluation of STALE versus INVALID; correct the failed-signature mapping.
decision_needed: What makes a binding STALE rather than INVALID, what is the full status vocabulary, and what stale-binding policy is the CLI default?

requirement_or_question: Frozen binding-status table: no change or Index rebuild keeps all VALID; codec, transform, dictionary, group, layout or ciphertext change with identical Chunk organization keeps content and physical VALID; mtime, Fidelity, AUX or content identity change stales content; rechunking stales physical; recipient add stales addressing; removal, password change or AFK rotation stales addressing and physical when keyed rechunk changes PCR.
implementation_evidence: Only add-recipient (addressing stale) and rotation LAI/AUX stability are tested (tests/crypto_v1.rs:213-314; cross-ref code-crypto-b-0099, code-crypto-b-0148).
research_needed: Conformance test per table row including repack, recompress, rechunk, metadata change and keyed rechunk; confirm PCR independence of codec and ciphertext (cross-ref docs-crypto-a-0175).

requirement_or_question: Legacy import validates every present integrity authority (7z packed, folder and substream CRCs; gzip CRC-32 and ISIZE; bzip2 CRC; zstd content checksum; xz checks; tar header checksum) and admits bytes to EAM only after all succeed. Checksum-less zstd frames are accepted, xz check and filter acceptance is delegated to lzma-rust2, and zstd structural and checksum errors share one code.
supersession_note: docs/compressed-stream-import-v1.md L31-32 and L36-39 claim frame checksums are enforced and unsupported checks fail; code enforces only checksums that are present.
implementation_evidence: legacy/stream.rs:237-248 gzip (test gzip_members_are_independently_verified_and_concatenated stream.rs:817-842); stream.rs:368-387 zstd optional checksum (test zstd_xz_and_bzip2_corruption_never_yields_accepted_plaintext stream.rs:916-952 uses checksummed frames only); stream.rs:441-451 xz delegated; stream.rs:516-558 bzip2; legacy/tar.rs:250-256,1398-1428 (test tar.rs:1939-1946).
research_needed: Fixtures: checksum-less zstd with corrupted literals; xz with check None, CRC32, SHA-256, BCJ x86 and delta; record acceptance and outcome class; consider reporting integrity-unverified layers.
decision_needed: Should strict import require content checksums or report integrity-unverified layers, and must strict XZ import refuse check=None?

requirement_or_question: A CRC-32 match is not proof of content identity: Research III measured a tuned CRC collision where 9-byte and 51-byte interpretations both match the header CRC. The Java ZipFile compatibility profile models CRC disagreement as unenforced and its safety overrides omit CRC mismatch, so CRC-failing content may enter the EAM.
implementation_evidence: Strict ZIP import has ZipCrcMismatch and ZipSizeMismatch codes (cross-ref code-legacy-a-0154); whether the java-zipfile profile imports CRC-mismatched content is unverified.
research_needed: Code review and fixtures of the java-zipfile profile with CRC mismatch; CRC-collision fixture through every profile confirming declared-size versus inflated-length mismatch is flagged.
decision_needed: Should CRC-32 verification and declared-size agreement be safety invariants for every compatibility profile?

requirement_or_question: Commands must never leave partial artifacts under final names: planning precedes output creation, publish stages exclusive temp siblings, syncs and hard-links with rollback, and convert removes failed outputs. INDEXED pack does not remove partial output on write failure, export writes directly at the final name so a crash leaves a partial target, and crashes mid-transaction leave temp siblings without recovery.
implementation_evidence: entrybound-cli/src/lib.rs:757-760 planning first (cli_workflow.rs:299-302 no output after refused STREAM window); lib.rs:809-841 INDEXED pack lacks cleanup; lib.rs:1114-1159 export; lib.rs:1564-1673 transactional_publish (rollback test lib.rs:5788-5800; blocked directory test lib.rs:5764-5786); lib.rs:2232-2257 convert cleanup.
research_needed: Fault injection (disk full, process kill between steps, simulated power loss) for pack INDEXED, export, publish, repack and sidecar; leftover detection.
decision_needed: Should all outputs use temp+sync+link/rename transactions, and is crash-leftover cleanup or recovery required?

requirement_or_question: All CLI output files are created exclusively; existing destinations are never overwritten and no --force option exists; running sidecar twice for the same source fails with EB_EXTRACT_COLLISION and leaves the source unchanged.
supersession_note: SPEC §11.6 Pattern 3 (cross-ref platform spec-05-0072) allows a caller --on-collision overwrite policy; code freezes refuse-only.
implementation_evidence: entrybound-cli/src/lib.rs:4952-4964; unit test deterministic_zip_tar_export_receipt_dry_run_and_reimport_workflow (lib.rs:5660-5675); sidecar collision test lib.rs:5837-5847.
research_needed: Usability evaluation of refuse-only outputs; TOCTOU analysis of exclusive create plus hard link.
decision_needed: Is 'never overwrite, no --force' the frozen v1 CLI policy versus SPEC's caller-selected --on-collision?

requirement_or_question: Key mutations and embedded signing replace archives through replace_verified: a synced verified temp, rename of the original to a backup, rename of the temp into place, then backup removal. Between renames no file exists at the original path, fixed per-PID temp and backup names fail when left over, and an undocumented --output writes a separate file.
implementation_evidence: entrybound-cli/src/lib.rs:2924-2972 (--output L2801-2807, L2874-2880); mutation output verified by crypto/container.rs:927-979.
research_needed: Crash injection between rename steps on NTFS and ext4; evaluate rename-over, renameat2 and ReplaceFileW.
decision_needed: Should in-place mutation use a platform atomic replace primitive, and is --output documented?
